league.name: Grand Northern Hockey League
league.founding: The Blizzard Charter: eight club owners snowbound for three days in the Hotel Lindell wrote the constitution on the back of a dinner menu.

trophy.name: Puckworth Cup
trophy.donor: Sir Reginald Puckworth, lumber baron, 1912; a silver punch bowl refused by the Kingsport Curling Club
trophy.deed: Awarded each year to the finest hockey club in the Dominion, and nobody may drink out of it.

eras.name: Frontier Era
eras.note: Seven-man hockey, outdoor ice, no forward pass; 1919 Cup not awarded (the Great Thaw).

eras.name: Wool Era
eras.note: Forward pass legalised 1929; Port Hollis and Ottershaw fold.

eras.name: Six Era
eras.note: Six clubs, Kingsport dynasty, maskless goalies.

eras.name: Great Expansion
eras.note: Granite City 1967; Trans-Prairie Hockey Association merger 1972 brings Redstone; the Lumber Years.

eras.name: Clutch Years
eras.note: Hooking and holding; Lake Ostrander joins 2001.

eras.name: Lost Winter
eras.note: Lockout, season cancelled; the Sandwich Clause; the Cup visits Millbrook for one night.

eras.name: Modern Era
eras.note: Salary cap, shootout, trapezoid; Silverton expansion 2018.

rivalries.name: The Highway 9 War
rivalries.note: 1977 brawl spilled into the parking lot

traditions: Frozen herring on the ice in Marrow Bay
Mittens thrown for hat tricks in Fairhaven

teams.name: Monarchs
teams.identity: Old money, the most Cups, the most insufferable fans, and an organist.

teams.name: Iron
teams.identity: A steel town club that wins ugly and is proud of it.

teams.name: Coureurs
teams.identity: Flair, speed and the oldest grudge in hockey.

teams.name: Foresters
teams.identity: Big, slow-to-anger lumber town team; they forget nothing.

teams.name: Gulls
teams.identity: Fishing port, frozen herring, the smartest front office in the league.

teams.name: Squalls
teams.identity: Coldest city, warmest fans, the mitten throw.

teams.name: Stonecutters
teams.identity: First expansion team, chip on the shoulder carved in granite.

teams.name: Rockets
teams.identity: Surviving rebels of the Trans-Prairie league; chrome helmets.

teams.name: Scorpions
teams.identity: Desert hockey; fans who learned the rules in 1994 and argue them best.

teams.name: Loons
teams.identity: Lovable, cursed, abbreviated LOL by accident; still waiting.

teams.name: Specters
teams.identity: Casino-town expansion team that won in year two and never stopped mentioning it.

players.name: Aurele Fontaine
players.reputation: The first superstar; the fastest skater of the outdoor age.

players.name: Hector MacInnes
players.reputation: The immovable defenceman; one Shorewood stick, one career (allegedly).

players.name: Walter Brzezinski
players.reputation: The greatest goalie of the Six Era; famously, foolishly maskless.

players.name: Jim Harrowgate
players.reputation: The cleanest great player who ever lived; still hated in Ste-Colette.

players.name: Denis Bellerose
players.reputation: The most stylish player of the seventies; the hair, the shot.

players.name: Moose Kowalczuk
players.nickname: The Mayor of the Penalty Box
players.reputation: All-time penalty minutes leader; now the most beloved man on television and the face of Brokenbone Mutual.

players.name: Ronnie Haverstock
players.reputation: The valley's own: Millbrook milk-truck driver turned star; invented the Millbrook bank pass; number 14 hangs in the Millbrook Community Arena.

players.name: Teddy Varga
players.reputation: The best there ever was; the subject of The Trade.

players.name: Barry Pomeroy
players.reputation: The most beloved journeyman in hockey; seven stints with the Duncannon Dukes; won his only Cup in his last game.

players.name: Ricky Delorme
players.reputation: The Wrong Twin scandal: his twin Donnie played 11 games for him in 1996; suspended a season.
players.note: Totals include 11 games and 6 goals by Donnie Delorme, with an asterisk.

players.name: Patrice Gendron
players.reputation: The butterfly master; talks to his goalposts; octopus mask.

players.name: Viktor Sokolov
players.reputation: Most hated agitator of his generation; three rules named after him; now a children's TV presenter.

players.name: Morris Teague
players.reputation: The payroll accountant and Harlow Falls beer leaguer who won the Cup as emergency backup.

players.name: Theo Lindgren-Baptiste
players.reputation: The modern superstar; never misses a shift; the analytics department's favourite person.

resurfacers.name: Zambelli Inc.
resurfacers.slogan: It Is a Zambelli Brand Ice Resurfacer.
resurfacers.logo: A chrome Z on a blue badge panel.

lines.name: Model 525
lines.note: The classic boxy machine: cream snow tank with blue band and pinstripe, chrome Z badge, twin headlamps, driver perched high on the left, engine cowl at the back, about 1.9 x 3.6 x 2 m, top speed about 14 km/h. Millbrook's 1974 unit is named Doris.

resurfacers.name: Flatley Ice Machines
resurfacers.founder: Walt Flatley, Zambelli's ex-partner and brother-in-law
resurfacers.logo: A green flat line with a towel drape under the word FLATLEY.

lines.name: Model 7
lines.note: drove in the 1966 Kingsport parade race

lines.name: Flatliner F-9
lines.note: died at centre ice in the 1972 Final: the Intermission That Lasted Forty Minutes

resurfacers.name: Polarix Ice Systems
resurfacers.logo: A white hexagon with a cyan laser line cutting across it.

lines.name: Polarix Glide
lines.note: refused to leave the ice for the Sunvale mascot in 2015

resurfacer_saga.wet_towel_patent: Filed by both Zambelli and Flatley in 1953; granted 1956, appealed 1957, overturned 1961, reinstated 1966, settled 1984 after it expired. Neither may claim to be the original; both advertise as the first.
resurfacer_saga.parade_incident: 1966 Kingsport Cup parade: Frank Zambelli and Walt Flatley raced side by side for six blocks at 14 km/h and ended in the Victoria Square fountain, with the Cup briefly in it too.
resurfacer_saga.genericide: Everyone calls every resurfacer a zambelli; Zambelli's lawyers write letters to dictionaries, broadcasters and a Kessler primary school (1982).
